Status: INCOMPLETE / verification not passed.

What I did: I edited `django/contrib/admin/options.py` in `BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed()`. My first attempt added a `parent_link` guard on `prev_field.remote_field`, which caused an `AttributeError` on reverse OneToOne relations; I then softened it with `getattr(..., "parent_link", False)`, which made the local `modeladmin` public selection pass (162 tests OK) but did NOT fix the host feature test `test_lookup_allowed_foreign_primary` (still `AssertionError: False is not True`).

Diagnosis of the remaining bug: the concrete-inheritance shortcut condition is
`prev_field.is_relation and field not in prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields`.
For `restaurant__place__country`, `place` IS in the FK `restaurant`'s `target_fields` (because `Restaurant.place` is the pk), so `place` is wrongly dropped from `relation_parts`, collapsing the lookup to `restaurant__country`. The guard must be based on whether the *current* `field` is an actual concrete-inheritance parent link (e.g. `field.remote_field.parent_link` / `field.one_to_one and field.remote_field.parent_link`), not on `prev_field`. My correction attempts to apply that change were rejected as "old_str equals new_str" (I mistakenly resubmitted unchanged text), and the public-test budget then ran out before I could land the corrected edit.

Current on-disk state: the file contains the reverted/original condition (the `getattr(prev_field.remote_field, "parent_link", False)` guard was removed), so the feature behavior is NOT fixed. No further edits or tests were possible within budget. The fix still needs to be applied: change the shortcut so it only skips a relation part when the current field is a concrete-inheritance parent link.
